questions.question: A tool call needs the user to confirm a destructive action before a stateless 2026-07-28 server can finish it. What happens?
options: The server blocks in place until a background worker resolves the confirmation for it
The server stores the call in memory and waits for a separate confirmation endpoint to eventually be hit
The server ends the call with an input_required result and the client retries as a new request
The server opens a stream and pushes a server-initiated request while the original call stays open
questions.explanation: MRTR replaces server-initiated requests: the server ends the original call with resultType input_required, and the client gathers input, then retries the request independently.

questions.question: When the client retries a tools/call after collecting the answers listed in inputRequests, what must be true of the JSON-RPC id?
options: It is left out entirely because the retry is answered on the original response stream
It reuses the id from the input_required response so the server can match up its state
It is chosen by the server and returned to the client inside requestState itself
It is a brand new id, because the retry counts as an independent request entirely
questions.explanation: The retry is a completely independent request, so its JSON-RPC id must differ from the id used on the original call that received input_required.

questions.question: What is a client required to do with the requestState field carried on an input_required result?
options: Echo it back on the retry exactly, without inspecting or altering its contents
Merge it into clientInfo so the server can read it back from a trusted field
Cache it alongside the tool definition so future calls can reuse the same value
Decode it locally to check whether the encoded expiry timestamp has already passed
questions.explanation: requestState is opaque to the client; the client must echo it back unchanged on the retry and must not parse, inspect, or modify it in any way.

questions.question: Which set of client requests may a server answer with an input_required result under MRTR?
options: Only requests that already carry a progressToken value inside their _meta block
tools/call, prompts/get, and resources/read, and nothing else at all in the protocol
Any client request, since input_required works as a general purpose pause signal here
Only server/discover, because it is treated as the sole protocol entry point for it
questions.explanation: Servers may send InputRequiredResult only on tools/call, prompts/get, and resources/read; every other client request must always finish as resultType complete.

questions.question: A retry's requestState carries a valid signature and has not expired, but it was minted for a different authenticated principal than the one presenting it now. What should the server do?
options: Accept it, since an unbroken HMAC signature already proves the state is trustworthy
Accept it only after asking the model to confirm the principal in plain text first
Reject it, because requestState stays bound to the one principal it was issued to
Accept it once, then flag the mismatch for a human to review during a later audit
questions.explanation: Integrity alone is not enough: requestState must be bound to the authenticated principal it was minted for, and a mismatch must be rejected even when the signature verifies.

questions.question: A deploy tool needs the user's payment card number before it can continue. How should it collect that value under 2026-07-28?
options: Skip elicitation and let the model infer a plausible value from the conversation
Place the request inside clientInfo so the client can prefill it for the model
Send a form mode elicitation/create request with a requestedSchema for the card fields
Use URL mode elicitation so the interaction stays outside the MCP client itself
questions.explanation: Servers must not use form mode for sensitive data such as payment credentials; URL mode elicitation keeps the interaction out of band so the value never transits the MCP client.
